client_alerts.headline: Google: Gmail, Drive and Photos content can now shape ad targeting
client_alerts.body: Newsletter coverage (Oct 25) says Google changed its privacy policy so that content from Gmail, Drive and Google Photos can help select ads when users connect those services to Gemini features. **Advise clients** to check whether staff use personal Google accounts with connected AI features for work material, and to confirm that Workspace (business) tenants are excluded before anyone relies on it.

client_alerts.headline: DeepSeek removal order for US federal civilian agencies
client_alerts.body: Reported alongside DeepSeek's ~$15B raise: federal civilian agencies were ordered to remove DeepSeek technology. Clients that sell to or support federal agencies should inventory DeepSeek models, apps and embedded 'powered by' components in their stack and in vendor products.

client_alerts.headline: Shadow-AI patient-data incident at a hospital
client_alerts.body: A Johns Hopkins Bayview notice (via daily digests, not primary-verified) describes a staffer uploading patient data to an unapproved public AI tool. A ready-made case study for client acceptable-use and data-loss-prevention reviews.

top_moves.title: Google lets connected Gmail/Drive/Photos content inform ads
top_moves.body: A privacy-policy change ties Gemini's connected-app features to ad selection. This is the biggest client data-risk change of the week for anyone mixing personal Google accounts with work content.

top_moves.title: DeepSeek raises ~$15B days after a US federal removal order
top_moves.body: The open-model geopolitics split hardens: federal civilian agencies must strip DeepSeek, Moonshot ships Kimi K3.1 open weights with cyberattack training data removed, and countries are being pushed to pick US or China AI blocs.

top_moves.title: Anthropic and Suno face ~$340M in music copyright suits
top_moves.body: New copyright exposure for Anthropic lands while its IPO is still pending, with no public S-1. Worth noting in vendor-risk sections of client AI assessments.

providers.name: OpenAI
providers.headline: No new dated release in the window; GPT-6 (Sol paid / Luna free), Slides in Spaces and PIN-locked chats (Oct 20) remain the current set.
providers.detail: GPT-6 shipped Oct 7–8 with Intelligent UI. Slides arrived in Spaces on Oct 16 and Locked chats began a gradual rollout on Oct 20. Enterprise access to GPT-6 depends on admin settings. Nothing new found for Oct 24–26.

providers.name: Anthropic
providers.headline: Named with Suno in ~$340M of music copyright suits; public S-1 still not filed.
providers.detail: Newsletter coverage (Oct 25) reports the combined copyright claims. The IPO track remains confidential since the June 1 draft S-1. No new model or product release found in the window; Claude Code continues frequent point builds.

providers.name: Google Gemini
providers.headline: Privacy policy now lets connected Gmail, Drive and Photos content inform ad selection.
providers.detail: The change applies when users connect those services to AI features. It follows the October tier squeeze (Free dropped to Flash-Lite Oct 9; Plus loses Pro on emailed dates). An unconfirmed 'Gemini 4 Argon' and Gems-to-skills migration also circulate in changelogs.
providers.alertReason: Consumer content used for ad targeting when AI features are connected

providers.name: xAI
providers.headline: Quiet; Grok 4.7 remains flagship and Grok 5 still has not shipped ahead of the Oct 31 market deadline.
providers.detail: Last dated release was Grok Voice 3.0 on Oct 14. Grok 4.7 (Sept 21, 500K context, $2/$6 per M tokens) is on Bedrock. Prediction markets still ask whether Grok 5 ships by Oct 31.

providers.name: Meta
providers.headline: No new release; Muse Spark remains Meta AI's model and no new open Llama has appeared.
providers.detail: Llama has effectively been replaced by Meta Superintelligence Labs' closed models since April. No October release found.

providers.name: Mistral
providers.headline: No new release; Large 4 preview (Oct 6) is still API-only with open weights promised.
providers.detail: Mistral Large 4 preview is available on the API; the open-weight release is said to follow in coming months. No further October news found.

providers.name: Perplexity
providers.headline: No dated release; publisher lawsuits (at least seven) remain the main story.
providers.detail: No October changelog found. Legal coverage notes at least seven publisher suits, with one ruling in Perplexity's favour.

providers.name: Microsoft 365 Copilot
providers.headline: No new message-center item; Copilot Home is in Frontier only and the in-app prompt box rolls out through December.
providers.detail: Chat and Cowork share a Home screen for Frontier users in October, not GA. The Word/Excel/PowerPoint Copilot-button prompt box rolls out Sept–Dec with no admin action. Suleyman's Oct 22 medical-AI claim is consumer/research, not M365.

providers.name: GitHub Copilot
providers.headline: No new release beyond the Computer Use preview covered yesterday; usage-based billing and share pressure persist.
providers.detail: Computer Use is in public preview in Copilot CLI and desktop apps. Usage-based billing with AI Credits since June 1. JetBrains survey share: Copilot 29%, Cursor 18%, Claude Code 18%.

providers.name: Cursor
providers.headline: No new release beyond 3.24's auto-review safety controls covered yesterday.
providers.detail: Cursor 3.24 added auto-review safety controls (secondary source). Nothing newer found for Oct 24–26.

providers.name: Gamma
providers.headline: No release found; the long quiet stretch continues.
providers.detail: No dated Gamma release notes found for October.

providers.name: Notion AI
providers.headline: No new release; Notion Workers credit billing (from Oct 15) is the last change.
providers.detail: No October release notes found beyond the Workers billing change.

month_themes.now: Consumer AI data feeding ad targeting; US/China split over open models (DeepSeek removal, Kimi K3.1); copyright liability for model vendors

watch.title: Grok 5 by Oct 31?
watch.body: Prediction markets close at month-end. A launch would be xAI's first new major version since Grok 4.x.

watch.title: DeepSeek removal scope
watch.body: Watch for whether the federal civilian order extends to contractors or other China-origin models such as Kimi.

watch.title: Gemini Plus loses Pro access
watch.body: Google is emailing Plus subscribers their dates. Clients relying on consumer Gemini Plus for Pro-model work should plan for Pro/Ultra or Workspace.

watch.title: Anthropic public S-1
watch.body: A listing was reportedly targeted for as soon as October; the copyright suits may appear in risk factors once the S-1 goes public.
